info.title: Machine to Machine Service API
info.description: API for machine-2-machine interaction with the EPO. **Welcome** Welcome to the swagger page of the "Machine-2-Machine" service in our production environment. \ **Sandbox environment (non-production)** A non-production environment is available for technical tests to companies that have registered their interest and have requested access. \ This service is made available through a "Sandbox" environment which contains dummy data only. \ To help you get started, we have prepared a set of examples of usage of the API in Python, Java and Javascript. \ You will find these examples [here](https://link.epo.org/web/EPO%20Mailbox%20API%20Sandbox%20Examples.zip). **Production environment** For integration with the EPO's production environment an explicit request for production client credentials needs to be made to support@epo.org. **Authentication** In order to use the API please follow OAuth 2.0 standard with the provided client credentials (client_id and Secret). \ As such, your IP Management System should first make a call to the EPO's authentication service using the provided credentials to obtain an access token. \ The obtained bearer access token can then be used in the second call to one of the various endpoints of the MyEPO "Machine to Machine" service. **For testing purposes and the use of this swagger page** Please use the URL of the EPO's authentication service [https://login.epo.org/oauth2/aus6hh2ns9ORf2PD3417/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server](https://login.epo.org/oauth2/aus6hh2ns9ORf2PD3417/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server) with the provided clientId and secret and ask for mailboxapi scope. \ Below you can find a command to create the bearer access_token using *curl* and the related sample output ``` curl --location 'https://login.epo.org/oauth2/aus6hh2ns9ORf2PD3417/v1/token' \ --header 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \ --data-urlencode 'grant_type=client_credentials' \ --data-urlencode 'client_id={CLIENT_ID}' \ --data-urlencode 'client_secret={SECRET}' \ --data-urlencode 'scope=mailboxapi' ``` **Sample Output** ``` { "access_token": "abc1234asdf9823...", "expires_in": 18000, "scope": "mailboxapi", "token_type": "Bearer" } ``` The value of the property access_token can be pasted in the bearerAuth input field shown when clicking on the "Authorize" button in this page. Once Authorised, endpoints can be triggered through this page. **How to get support or to provide feedback** If you need help or would like to provide feedback, please send an email to our support desk: support@epo.org **ChangeLog** The change log can be found here. **Standards** The API is implementing ST90 standards except the following points: - The API does not support RSG[21-27] in regards to providing XML representation of the resource - The API does not support RSG[100] in regards to specifying request timeout by the client - The API does not support RSG[101-104,107] in regards to supporting caching of the resource - The API does not support RSG[107] in regards to providing sending large files in chunks

get.summary: Get due dates for an application.
get.description:
### **Authorization** The company administrator has to set grant the B2B account permission to the portfolio (in which the application is present) of the representative or association.
This is done in the permission area in MyEPO (More information can be found [here](https://link.epo.org/web/myepo-services/interact/en-myepo-portfolio-feature-guide-managing-user-access.pdf)).
In case the B2B account is not authorized to access the portfolio, the following error message will appear:
response code 403 ``` { "code": "ERR_20", "message": "User is not authorised to perform this action." } ``` ### **Parameters** | Field | Description | |---------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | **{procedure}** | Allowed values:
- `EPC`
- `UPP` | | **{application}** | Identifier of the patent application.
Format: `EPYYNNNNNN` | ### **Response** - The response will contain a “termkey”. The description of this “termkey” can can be retrieved with the API GET ../terms. - At the moment no terms are returned for applications in your portfolio for which you are effectively representing the Opponent. ### **Point of attention** Today there is no direct link between a time limit/due date and a communication.
As an alternative:
After downloading a communication, the API /latest/{procedure}/applications/{application}/dueDates can be called for the application.
This will provide an overview of all the time limits/due dates for the application (within the EPC or UPP). ### **Sandbox environment** To test the API, the following procedures and application numbers are available in the Sandbox environment: - Procedure type “EPC” – Application “EP00000001” - Procedure type “EPC” – Application “EP00000002” - Procedure type “EPC” – Application “EP00000003” - Procedure type “UPP” – Application “EP00000001” - Procedure type “UPP” – Application “EP00000008”

get.summary: Get portfolios for which the account is authorised
get.description:
### **Authorization**
- If the B2B account is defined as a company admin, all the portfolio id’s of the company are returned.
- If the B2B account has permission on a portfolio, the portfolio ID is returned.
- In case the B2B account is not allowed to access any portfolio an empty list is returned
The company administrator has to set grant the B2B account permission to the portfolio of the representative or association. This is done in the permission area in MyEPO (More information can be found [here](https://link.epo.org/web/myepo-services/interact/en-myepo-portfolio-feature-guide-managing-user-access.pdf)).

get.summary: Get bibliographical data for an application number
get.description:
### **Authorization** The company administrator has to set grant the B2B account permission to the portfolio (in which the application is present) of the representative or association. This is done in the permission area in MyEPO (More information can be found [here](https://link.epo.org/web/myepo-services/interact/en-myepo-portfolio-feature-guide-managing-user-access.pdf)).\ In case the B2B account is not authorized to access the portfolio, the following error message will appear:\ response code 403 ``` { "code": "ERR_20", "message": "User is not authorised to perform this action." } ``` Notes: - In case the application is in your portfolio as you are effectively representing the Opponent, the error message "User is not authorised to perform this action" will appear. - The bibliographic data can only be retrieved for applications part of a portfolio within your company. ### **Parameters:** | Field | Description | |------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | **{procedure}** | Allowed values:
- `EPC` | | **{application}**| Identifier of the patent application. Format:
- `EPYYNNNNNN` | ### **Response** - The response will contain the publication information after the distribution of communication 1133. ### **Sandbox environment** To test the API, the following procedures and application numbers are available in the Sandbox environment: - Procedure type “EPC” – Application “EP00000001” - Procedure type “EPC” – Application “EP00000002” - Procedure type “EPC” – Application “EP00000003” - Procedure type “EPC” – Application “EP00000008”

The company administrator has to set grant the B2B account permission to the portfolio (in which the application is present) of the representative or association.  This is done in the permission area in MyEPO (More information can be found [here](https://link.epo.org/web/myepo-services/interact/en-myepo-portfolio-feature-guide-managing-user-access.pdf)).\
In case the B2B account is not authorized to access the portfolio, the following error message will appear:\
response code 403
```
{
  "code": "ERR_20",
  "message": "User is not authorised to perform this action."
}
```

### **Response**
Please note: Applications for which you are effectively representing the Opponent are not returned.

### **Known issues**
- Link Get Biblio - procedure {UPP}\
  It is currently not yet possible to retrieve the bibliographic data for an application within the UPP procedure.\
  Starting the API with the link included in the response  will return an error message.\
  This feature will be made available in a future release.

bearerAuth.description:
In order to use the API please follow OAuth 2.0 standard with the provided client credentials (client_id and Secret). \
As such, your IP Management System should first make a call to the EPO's authentication service using the provided credentials to obtain an access token. \
The obtained bearer access token can then be used in the second call to one of the various endpoints of the MyEPO "Machine to Machine" service. 

**For testing purposes and the use of this swagger page** 

Please use the URL of the EPO's authentication service [https://login.epo.org/oauth2/aus6hh2ns9ORf2PD3417/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server](https://login.epo.org/oauth2/aus6hh2ns9ORf2PD3417/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server) with the provided clientId and secret and ask for mailboxapi scope. \
Below you can find a command to create the bearer access_token using *curl* and the related sample output
```
curl --location 'https://login.epo.org/oauth2/aus6hh2ns9ORf2PD3417/v1/token' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  --data-urlencode 'grant_type=client_credentials' \
  --data-urlencode 'client_id={CLIENT_ID}' \
  --data-urlencode 'client_secret={SECRET}' \
  --data-urlencode 'scope=mailboxapi'
```
**Sample Output**
```
{
  "access_token": "abc1234asdf9823...",
  "expires_in": 18000,
  "scope": "mailboxapi",
  "token_type": "Bearer"
}
```
The value of the property access_token can be pasted in the bearerAuth input field shown when clicking on the "Authorize" button in this page. 
Once Authorised, endpoints can be triggered through this page.
